finding.question: Is the US Fox News Channel available to television subscribers in Canada as of the investigation date?
finding.summary: Yes. In August 2020, Canadian broadcasting trade publication Cartt.ca reported that the main American Fox News channel was carried by many Canadian television distributors. The CRTC had approved the non-Canadian Fox News service for digital distribution in 2004; a contemporaneous Rogers announcement said it had added the US channel to its lineup. This evidence concerns Fox News Channel, not the separately proposed Fox News Canada service or Fox’s international streaming service.

finding.question: Does Canadian law, specifically the Radio Act, make lying to the public via the airwaves a crime?
finding.summary: The evidence does not support a broad criminal prohibition under a Radio Act against lying over the airwaves. Broadcasting regulations prohibited licensees from broadcasting false or misleading news; in 2011, the CRTC decided not to narrow those provisions. Separately, the Supreme Court struck down the Criminal Code’s false-news provision as unconstitutional in 1992.

finding.question: What evidence links Canadian law or regulatory decisions about false broadcast news to the authorization or distribution of the US Fox News Channel in Canada?
finding.summary: The CRTC authorized the US Fox News service for digital distribution in Canada in November 2004, finding that it was not competitive with a Canadian pay or specialty service. CBC reported that an earlier application had been rejected because a Canadian Fox News service was planned; that separate project did not proceed. The CRTC later confirmed that its false-or-misleading-news provisions remained unchanged in 2011. The cited records do not support a false-news rule as the reason for excluding Fox News.

sources.title: Broadcasting Public Notice CRTC 2004-88
sources.snippet: The Commission approves the addition of the non-Canadian services, Fox News and NFL Network, to its lists of eligible satellite services for distribution on a digital basis. ... In light of the above, the Commission is of the view that neither Fox News nor the NFL Network is partially or totally competitive with any Canadian pay or specialty service. Accordingly, the Commission approves the requests by the CCTA to add Fox News and the NFL Network to the digital lists.

sources.title: CRTC approves Fox News for Canada
sources.snippet: The CRTC rejected a CCTA application to bring Fox to Canada last November because Fox News U.S. and Winnipeg-based Global Television were planning to create Fox News Canada, a combination of U.S. and Canadian news.

sources.title: Broadcasting Public Notice CRTC 2004-45
sources.snippet: The CCTA attached to its request a letter dated 31 March 2004 from Fox News, the non-Canadian partner in Fox News Canada. In that letter, Fox News addressed the Fox News Canada service as follows: "Fox News does not intend to implement this service and therefore will not meet the extended deadline to commence operations."

sources.title: Broadcasting Regulatory Policy CRTC 2011-455
sources.snippet: the Commission announced in Broadcasting Regulatory Policy 2011-308 that it would not amend the false or misleading news provisions set out in various Commission regulations. As a result, section 3(d) of the Radio Regulations; section 5(1)(d) of the Television Broadcasting Regulations; section 3(2)(c) of the Pay Television Regulations; and section 3(d) of the Specialty Services Regulations, remain unchanged.

caveats: Authorization permits distribution but does not establish that every Canadian provider carried Fox News, or establish its carriage status on the reference date.
The cited explanation for the 2003 rejection is contemporaneous independent reporting rather than the original decision.

report_raw.claim: Fox News is unavailable in Canada because the Radio Act makes it a crime to lie to the public via airwaves.
report_raw.justification: In August 2020, a Canadian broadcasting trade publication reported that many Canadian distributors carried the main US Fox News channel. [S1] The CRTC had authorized its digital distribution in Canada in 2004. [S2] Canadian broadcasting regulations did restrict false or misleading news, and the CRTC retained those provisions in 2011. [S4][S5][S9] But the evidence does not establish the claimed broad criminal prohibition under a Radio Act, and Canada’s separate Criminal Code false-news provision was struck down as unconstitutional. [S6][S9] Inference: The reported carriage and regulatory approval contradict the claim that such a law made Fox News unavailable in Canada. [S1][S2]
key_points: The US Fox News channel was reported to be carried by many Canadian distributors shortly before the reference date. [S1]
The CRTC approved Fox News for digital distribution in 2004. [S2]
False-or-misleading-news provisions existed in broadcasting regulations, not as the broad Radio Act crime described in the claim. [S4][S5][S9]
An earlier application was rejected because a Canadian Fox News service was planned, according to contemporaneous reporting. [S7]
report_raw.counter_argument: A case for a narrower reading is that Canadian broadcasting regulations did prohibit licensees from broadcasting false or misleading news, and an earlier application to bring Fox News to Canada was rejected. [S5][S7][S9] But the reported reason for that rejection was a planned Canadian service, not a false-news rule; the US channel was subsequently approved and reported to be carried in Canada. [S1][S2][S7]
evidence_gaps: A Canadian provider’s own channel listing from the reference date would further corroborate the August 2020 trade report.
The supplied official legal sources do not give a complete account of penalties for breaching the broadcasting regulations or directly document the full scope of the purported Radio Act.

As a result, section 3(d) of the Radio Regulations; section 5(1)(d) of the Television Broadcasting Regulations; section 3(2)(c) of the Pay Television Regulations; and section 3(d) of the Specialty Services Regulations, remain unchanged.
